summary: Linda Learman specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral work under supervisor Robert P. Weller (attested 2005) and postdoctoral study under mentor Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).

Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 1993, served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983), and taught Margarita Angelica Delgado Creamer.
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under MA supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas as well as teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan.
Lindy Li Mark is an anthropologist and sinologist who held positions as professor of anthropology at California State University, East Bay, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Ling Ji is a sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under the doctoral supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1968–1972), later serving on the faculty at the University of Tartu from circa 1969 to 2010.

Lionel David Barnett studied at Liverpool and Cambridge. An Indologist, he served as Keeper at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), Professor of Sanskrit at UCL (1906–1917), and Lecturer in Ancient Indian History and Epigraphy at SOAS (1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia earned his PhD at the University of Lille (1997). A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, he held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2.

Liqian Liu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the State Council translation administration department (~1952–1959), and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1959–1978).

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held positions at Stanford University (attested 1996) and served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995 and completed her MA and PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko.
Lita Peipina works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Oslo (MA attested 2008) under MA supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and also studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Litian Fang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. He studied at Peking University (~1956–1961) under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian, and served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University (~1961–2014).

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).
Lobsang Dargyay was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and the University of Munich, where he earned a Dr.phil. (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959). He founded the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (serving as head ~1973–1997) and the College for Higher Tibetan Studies.

Lobsang Jamspal, a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Columbia University under Alex Wayman. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, University of Delhi, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University.
Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and other teachers, and taught John W. Pettit.

Lobsang Shastri is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin studied at Drepung and Gyuto Monasteries. A Tibetologist, he directed the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1988–2000), served as Chief Editor for Bibliotheca Indo-Tibetica Series (~1977–2001), and held leadership posts at several Central Schools for Tibetans.
